subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 42-year-old man is evaluated for 3 weeks of nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. He recently moved to a rural area and has been drinking water from a private well. Examination shows hyperpigmented macules on the trunk and a prolonged QT interval on ECG; his breath has a faint garlic odor. Serum lactate is 3.2 mmol/L, and urine alpha-ketoglutarate is elevated.
question: Decreased activity of which of the following TCA cycle enzymes best explains these findings?
explanation_correct: Arsenic binds to lipoic acid, a cofactor shared by the alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex and the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, so alpha-ketoglutarate accumulates and the TCA cycle slows. The resulting energy deficit and oxidative stress explain the gastrointestinal, cutaneous, and cardiac (QT prolongation) findings of chronic arsenic poisoning.

explanation_incorrect.A: Citrate synthase catalyzes the first step of the cycle (oxaloacetate plus acetyl-CoA to citrate) and is not a lipoic acid-dependent enzyme.
explanation_incorrect.B: Isocitrate dehydrogenase produces alpha-ketoglutarate; its inhibition would lower, not raise, alpha-ketoglutarate.
explanation_incorrect.C: Succinate dehydrogenase is an FAD-linked inner membrane enzyme (complex II) that does not use lipoic acid.
explanation_incorrect.E: Malate dehydrogenase catalyzes the final NADH-producing step of the cycle and is not lipoic acid dependent.

educationalObjective: Arsenic inhibits the lipoic acid-dependent alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, causing accumulation of alpha-ketoglutarate and impaired TCA cycle flux.
